item.title: Women's Circle: What We Carry - Honoring our Ancestors — Fri Oct 30, 6:30 PM — Yoga Mechanics at 107 Forest Street
item.description:
Women’s Circle is a monthly gathering for women to come together in a supportive, intentional space. New participants are always welcome. We suggest bringing a journal and a small object that reflects the month’s theme: What We Carry – Honoring our Ancestors. This might be a photo, token, or meaningful item that helps ground your experience. Not sure what to expect? We’ll circle up with other identifying women for guided conversation, reflection, and ritual. With Connie’s facilitation, the evening is designed to help you reconnect with yourself and with one another. Expect to leave feeling refreshed, grounded, and supported as you move through the season ahead. Financial Assistance is available. item.title: Nidra Night Guided Meditation w/ Hana Konheim - Day of the Dead Edition! — Sun Nov 1, 6:00 PM — Yoga Mechanics at 107 Forest Street
item.description:
Nidra Nights invites you to let go, release and immerse yourself in deep relaxation. This special edition of Nidra Night will honor of Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead). The evening will invite reflection on the cycles of rest & renewal, life & death. Costumes are welcome! In this special offering, we’ll explore the space between worlds, between sleep and awake, rest and renewal. Through a 40–45 minute guided Yoga Nidra practice, we’ll settle into deep rest while remaining gently aware. Join us in person or online. item.description:

item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Nov 11, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Youth Mental Health First Aid Training for ADULTS - November 2026 — Thu Nov 19, 12:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Youth Mental Health First Aid is designed for adults who regularly interact with young people ages 12–18. It teaches parents, caregivers, family members, teachers, school staff, and other caring adults how to recognize and respond to mental health or substance use challenges and support a young person who may be experiencing a crisis. The Course will:
Introduce common mental health challenges for youth Review typical adolescent development Teach a 5-step action plan for how to help young people in both crisis and non-crisis situations

item.title: Winter Sowing Workshop — Sat Nov 21, 2:00 PM — Glen Ridge - Meeting Room
item.description:
The Glen Ridge Public Library native seed free library will open in mid-November with free seeds. Planting native plants, leaving the leaves, and not using pesticides is a huge help to native insects and the birds that rely upon them to rear their young. Winter sowing of the free seeds available through the library is an easy, low cost way to add native plants to your landscaping. In this free workshop we will explain how to prepare your native seeds to they are ready to grow next spring. This process is called cold stratification, which will be explained with a how-to demonstration of various methods you can use. Thanksgiving to early January is the perfect time to winter sow seeds and start the cold stratification process. We will also answer questions about the seeds in the library and make recommendations on which plants you might wish to grow.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10286
